source.repro: `node browser-tests/probe-maf-column-cap.ts 464 3` in products/jbrowse-web. Plain node, no browser: it calls `clusterMatrix` -- the same tail the MAF, variant, wiggle and multi-row-feature clustering RPCs all end in -- against @gmod/hclust 5.1.0. One warm-up call per column count discards the wasm instantiation, then three timed calls with the min reported.
source.notes: Synthetic, and the generator is the load-bearing part: ONE per-base truth is drawn at 20,000 columns and every row of the table is that same alignment re-binned by block-averaging, which is what MAX_COLUMNS varies. Drawing a fresh random matrix per column count instead compares different cohorts and reports ~0% adjacency and rho ~0 at every resolution, which is a property of the generator and not of the cap -- that was the first run of this probe and it is wrong. Rows carry a per-row divergence offset plus dropout runs (20-220 columns) so that which haplotype drops out where is real structure. Agreement is scored against the 20,000-column order, so the 100% and 1.000 on that row are by construction, not a result. Adjacency is a strict metric on 464 near-tied rows; read the monotone trend, not any single cell. AMD gcn-4 box, load average under 1. The docstring this replaces claimed 512 -> 5000 was 'minutes of worker time for a tree that comes out the same'; it was written 2026-08-17 against @gmod/hclust 5.0.0, a week before 5.1.0 took a further 2.5x on the distance build.
